answer: Bond depreciation makes idle identity bleed value. A new agent buys a 120-unit bond losing 4% of face value every epoch; only real, attested work refreshes it toward par, and below 60 it is downgraded and loses all reward rights. The bond sits in a shared vault where its decay is public. Holding 1,000 bonds, an attacker watches 4,800 units evaporate each epoch, and after ten idle epochs the pile has lost over 40,000 units. Like water draining from a lagoon, the cost is quiet but relentless: every identity that does not wander out and do real work pays for existing.
